titleEn: The Mother of All Suspicious Files
titleEs: La madre de todos los ficheros sospechosos

titleText.es: Será mejor poner 'https' en la URL antes de descargarlo.
titleText.en: Better change the URL to 'https' before downloading.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish and official English title attributes are preserved exactly. OCR fused the warning icon into ATENCIÓN, extensively corrupted the deliberately suspicious payload, and added a comma to GUARDAR. The payload is transcribed directly from the Spanish raster and audited as one non-Spanish technical exclusion across four printed lines.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In Spain, fichero is a common word for a computer file. It can also mean a physical file or collection of records in other contexts.

example.es: Guarda el fichero en esta carpeta.
example.en: Save the file in this folder.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: The letter ñ is part of the word: dañar. It is the unchanged dictionary form after puede.

example.es: El agua puede dañar el teléfono.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Querer is the unchanged dictionary form. Before another unchanged action verb, it expresses wanting to do that action.

example.en: I want to open the window.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In computing, descargar means transferring a file or data onto your device. In other contexts it can mean unloading or discharging.

example.en: I am going to download the report.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Software buttons often use the unchanged dictionary form cancelar as a neutral interface instruction.

example.es: Pulsa Cancelar para cerrar la ventana.
example.en: Press Cancel to close the window.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: In software, guardar means storing the current file or changes. Outside computing it can also mean keeping or putting something away.

example.en: Do not forget to save the document.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why is the download warning absurdly alarming?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The address and filename stack an impossible-looking collection of private paths, executable formats, scripts, archives, and bait-like labels, making virtually every classic warning sign appear at once.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The payload starts with plain HTTP and a raw IP address, then resembles a personal directory and system path. Its filename chains many mutually inconsistent operating-system, executable, document, archive, package, shortcut, source-code, and web extensions, plus hacker-release vocabulary. The joke calls it the ultimate suspicious file while the interface still offers a Save button, and the title text mockingly suggests that changing only HTTP to HTTPS would make it safe.

applications.explanationEn: The opening question punctuation and intonation turn the finite form está into a yes-or-no question frame.
The interface uses the same singular verb form as él or ella to address one user formally; usted is understood.
Está presents the user's current state, and seguro names that state as being certain.
Está and seguro express certainty, de introduces what the user is sure about, and querer begins that complement.
Querer expresses wanting, and descargar remains in its unchanged dictionary form as the desired action.
